courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media and Everyday Life
courses.description:
(GENA3070 is double-coded with COMM1110.)

Modern media are everywhere; they mediate nearly all aspects of everyday life. Media forms old and new – newspapers, magazines, films, radio, television, pop music, Internet, social media, and mobile phones – are shaping our social and political life, cultivating our cultural imaginations, and articulating our personal experiences and a sense of belonging in a rapidly changing world. This course examines the many roles of the media in the web of modern life.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students should:

1. Be equipped with enhanced media literacy.

2. Be able to understand the “operational logic” of different mass media and be able t to recognize the key issues related to media production.

3. Be able to apply theoretical concepts to analyze various media phenomena, especially towards the local mass media.

4. Students are able to understand the role mass media played in a post-modern society and to develop critical and analytical capabilities to evaluate and consume the media products.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Development of Media and Communication
courses.description: This course aims to offer an overview of the development of media and communication. It examines the various technological, political, economic and cultural factors that contributed to the rise and development of modern media. Students will develop a deeper and critical understanding of why mass communication has become what it is now. The course also encourages students to reflect on their roles as learners and future practitioners in the field of media and communication.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of the course, students will be able to:

1. Identify and describe major milestones in the history of mass communication.

2. Analyze the role of communication technologies in shaping media environments across different historical periods.

3. Examine the functions and significance of various storytelling forms within media genres.

4. Demonstrate an understanding of the economic development of media institutions and organizations.

5. Engage in critical discussions about the interconnections between the past, present, and future of media and communication.

6. Reflect on the significance of media literacy in contemporary society.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Introduction to Media Industries and Practices
courses.description: In the latter half of the 20th century, working in the media and communication industries referred mainly to working for newspapers, broadcasting stations, film companies, and advertising or PR industries. But with the advance of digital media technologies, old boundaries among the distinctive media sectors are seemingly blurring or even falling apart, while there might also be new types of “media companies.” This course is designed to familiarize students with the evolving realities of the various media industries in Hong Kong, China, and beyond. The overarching questions to be discussed in the class include: How can one characterize the configuration of the contemporary media industries? What are the key trends underlying the transformation of the media industries? What are the implications of these transformations for “media workers”? What does it mean by working as a journalist, a creative content producer, an advertiser, etc. in the contemporary world and in the future? What are the communication practices involved in the various industries? What are the broader social, cultural, and political implications of the transformation of media work and media industries?
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the semester, students will be able to:

- Acquire an overall understanding of the configuration of the contemporary media industries

- Analyze the continual evolution of the media industries and media work

- Better position themselves in terms of possible future career choices

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media and Social Development in Mainland China
courses.description:
(UGEC2634 is double-coded with COMM2140.)

The course is designed around two major themes, namely media and social development in Mainland China since the founding of the People's Republic in 1949. Using key concepts and theories from the political economy of media and developmental communication studies, it introduces students to different periods of media reform and social change from the era of Chairman Mao to the period of "harmonious society". Emphasis is attached to post-1989 media regulatory systems, media industrialization, and their influence on the meeting of such developmental goals as poverty alleviation, democratization, and communication empowerment.

The course will examine Mainland China's key media sectors including the printing press (newspapers and magazines), film and broadcasting media (radio and TV), and new networked communication tools (Internet and mobile phone) as well as alternative social formations through Internet activism, non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and transnational developmental projects. The course will identify and discuss several ongoing debates, and the ensuing actions, held by different stakeholders, including governmental officials, media producers, educators, activists, international agencies, and the general audiences. Wider implications to public policy will be identified. There will also be discussions of current affairs related to media and social development in the country.

Students will be able to describe the key characteristics of contemporary Mainland Chinese media and their roles in facilitating or obstructing development towards the ideals of a "new China".
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students will be able to describe key characteristics of media in Mainland China.

2. Students will be able to discuss how media influences social development and how new social formations trigger media reform in Mainland China.

3. Students will be able to identify phases of media and social development in Mainland China and differentiate policymaking rationales in different media sectors (printing, broadcasting, networked media) and types of social movements.

4. Students will be able to discuss competing arguments about the role of media reform in China's modernization drive.

5. Students will be able to produce a media text that offers a critique to one of the historical periods, media industries, or controversial issues covered in the course.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: News and Society
courses.description:
(UGEC2623 is double-coded with COMM2210.)

This course talks about the characteristics and functioning of news, and its important role and functions in society. News is vital to us as it brings latest information of the day, helps create public opinion, educate our young generations, monitor the government and the powerful, as well as provide relaxation to our busy lives. To understand the news can essentially help us know our society. Various concepts and theories from the mass communication discipline are introduced together with some perspectives from other social sciences. Real-life examples from Hong Kong and abroad are analyzed.

Students are first introduced to the unique nature of news and different types of news as found in both print and electronic media. Some new news formats, including free dailies, online newspapers, network social media and citizen journalism, are discussed in both international and local contexts. Relationships between journalism and closely related professions such as advertising and public relations are explicated in order to understand the actual functioning of news, as well as its impact on society. The professional concerns of the field of journalism and individual’s news consumption habits are also highlighted in the course.

After taking this course, students will be able to understand more about news and its relationship with the society. They should be able to critically evaluate news and social phenomena. It is hoped that they can become wise news consumers and well-informed citizens.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken COMM2910/UGEC2621 or UGEC2623.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will be able to describe the nature and characteristics of news.
Students will know about current affairs and can differentiate different types of news and their impacts.
Students will be equipped with news analytical skills and can apply them to study major news phenomena competently.
Students will be able to explore the role of news in society and discuss the relationship between news and society.
Students will be trained as wise news consumers and critical citizens.

Second, how are meanings created in mediated communication processes and what is the role of citizens and consumers in this process? Third, how do media and communication relate to critical issues such as social inequality and social justice? Why might the media be deemed to contribute to certain problems? Many of the theories covered in this course were developed in different traditions which have wide-ranging implications for our understanding of media and communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Social Media and Crisis Communication
courses.description:
(UGEC2636 is double-coded with COMM2813.)

With the advent of the new media technology, new forms of organizational crisis emerge. They are called Internet-mediated crises. A major difference between the Internet-mediated crises and the traditional crises lies in the intensive interactivity, collectivity, simultaneity and dialogic sphericity of the former. This very nature of Internet-mediated crisis makes it all the more hard to handle. A specialized and critical function of the public relations practice is the management of crisis.

This course covers two major levels. The first level takes on a functionalism approach to crisis management. The second level takes on a more critical approach in public relations. Students will learn how crisis reflects complicity and dynamism between citizens and organizations in modern societies. They will acquire an enhanced appreciation of communication that can be brought to bear in such crisis situations and a greater familiarity with the interactivity of an organization and its stakeholders as well as the environments in times of crises. They will also gain more sensitivity in public demands of socially responsible practices in the business contexts.

In this course, students will analyze real life campaigns to understand major effects of advertising in everyday life. Students will examine topics like materialism and commercialization of friendship to see how advertising persuade consumers through subtle uses of messages. They will also decode the formation and shifting of values promoted by Government and green campaigns. The course will help students distinguish between authentic and mediated reality regarding topics on artificial perfection of body image, sexual objectification and gender stereotyping.
courses.learning_outcomes:

1. Identify the multifaceted effects of mass-mediated advertising messages along the dimensions of subliminal messaging, infusion of constructed meanings, and mediation of reality.

2. Recognize the impacts of advertising on personal and psychological development.

3. Critically analyze advertising messages and motivations.

4. Investigate beyond the seemingly superficial phenomenon created by advertising into deeper issues related to living attitude and social values.

5. Develop a curiosity towards real life campaigns that promote meaningful causes that benefit citizens in Hong Kong.

By the end of the course, students should be able to:

1. understand and implement various editing techniques.

2. critically evaluate the functions and limitations of editing, and thus have a more holistic understanding of video/film production.

3. creatively present their ideas through video.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Understanding Movies
courses.description:
(UGED2637 is double-coded with COMM2930.)

This course aims at helping students to earn a solid vocabulary and a sharp eye in analyzing films. Students will learn about the basic cinematic techniques and structures, including mise-en-scene and montage, use of cinematic time and space, the image, soundtrack, and the script. Theoretical perspectives such as realism, feminism, postmodernism would be introduced to address the political, economic and socio-cultural implications of movies. Equipped with these analytical tools, students can critically appreciate movies of different era and different places.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken UGEC2643.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students will be able to develop cine-literacy and analyze movies through the comprehension of film languages.

2. Students will be able to relay the movies to their broader contexts of production and consumption and through which to understand the culturaldiversity.

3. Students will be able to critically reflect upon ideologies underlying the film texts.

4. Students will be able to discuss existing and emergent challenges facing by human world through the discussion of the relationship of movies and current thoughts such as feminism and post-modernism.

5. Students will be able to produce a critical film analysis that reflects upon political, social and cultural issues embedded in film texts.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Film Genres: Love, Death and Laughs
courses.description:
(GESC2010 is double-coded with COMM2932.)
This course focuses on a variety of film genres, such as detective and gangster film, musicals, comedies, family dramas and westerns. Genres have been popular since the beginning of the film medium and remain quite popular today. This class will examine the cultural and economic reasons for their continuing popularity. Film showings and film clips will demonstrate how genres evolve over time and how some of the great film directors have made genre films of lasting impact. This class assumes no prior knowledge of film. Students will be assessed on the basis of a paper and an examination.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Be the end of the course, students should:
1. Be knowledgeable about different film genres.
2. Be knowledgeable about the history and development of film genres.
3. Be able to examine how film forms are related to content as well as to culture.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Internet, Digital Media and Information Society
courses.description:
(UGEC2624 is double-coded with COMM2940.)

This course aims to examine a number of key issues that are closely related to developments in Internet and digital media. The advent of communication technologies has brought tremendous changes to media environments. Media convergence and participatory culture are two most notable emerging trends that have contributed to new forms of media production and consumption. Students will be introduced to key concepts and perspectives in appreciating, analyzing and evaluating such trends. Through case studies about social media, streaming entertainment, Internet celebrities, networked social movements and digital surveillance culture, etc, students will review the many tacit assumptions about Internet in their everyday life.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Photography
courses.description: This course combines a basic introduction to the practical skills of photography with an introduction to the idea of visual literacy - a look at the history and social role of the image in the contemporary image-driven multimedia environment.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken COMM2440.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. Demonstrate a critical understanding of fundamental creative principles of photography.

2. Demonstrate a sound knowledge in using digital SLR cameras and basic digital processing skills for images.

3 Appreciate and analyze the implications of different genres of photography.

4. Demonstrate an ability to formulate photographic concepts in daily practice.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Film, Television and Hong Kong Culture
courses.description:
(UGEC3635 is double-coded with COMM3191.)

Since the 1970s, a very distinctive Hong Kong culture has emerged. The course will focus on the role of film and television in the historical formation of this vibrant Hong Kong culture. It will also explore themes such as re-nationalization, nostalgia and representations of mainlanders after the sovereignty transfer in 1997.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students will be able to describe key characteristics of Hong Kong films and television in different historical periods.
2. Students will be able to discuss the influences and limitations of mass media in fostering collective identity.
3. Students will be able to differentiate between key concepts such as local and national identities, media representations and social practices, etc.
4. Students will be able to discuss competing viewpoints about the complicated relations between collective memories, cultural identity, and media representations.
5. Students will be able to produce a term paper that offers a critique to one of the ten issues covered in the course.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media and Gender
courses.description:
(UGEC3612 is double-coded with COMM3193.)

The course is developed and evolved around two major themes, namely mass media and gender. Using key concepts and theories in mass communication and cultural studies, it discusses the influences and power of mass media with an emphasis on gender-related issues. The latter are in turn related to other social and cultural phenomena that will bring in knowledge and perspectives from other disciplines (e.g. sociology and psychology).

The course will examine several recurring controversies related to gender in mass media. These controversies range from representation of sex and gender in media, to the media portrayals of homosexuals and the treatment of taboos. The course will identify and discuss the many competing viewpoints, and the ensuing actions, held by different stakeholders, including media producers, social activists, government regulators, educators and the general audiences. Their implications to legislation and education will also be identified.

Students will be able to describe the key characteristics of modern media, in particular their roles in the construction of gender identities and discourses about various gender issues.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students will be able to describe key characteristics of mass media.

2. Students will be able to discuss the influences and power of mass media in our society.

3. Students will be able to differentiate between such concepts as pornography and erotica, masculinity and femininity, etc.

4. Students will be able to discuss competing viewpoints about gender in the media.

5. Students will be able to produce a media text that offers a critique to one of the issues covered in the course.

courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

1. gain good knowledge of the essential concepts of media ethics and law, and its application through case studies.

2. reflect upon work related issues from a journalist’s perspective after comparative study of case laws in class on the topics that would cover important media ethical problems and legal issues.

3. acquire a better understanding of the vital values in media ethics and importance of major media laws that have significant bearing on journalists and news reporting.

2. Be able to work with reporters to come up with story ideas and develop stories for publication.

courses.subject: COMM

courses.description: This course is designed to provide training on the basic techniques of social media analytics with Python. It covers a variety of methods and tools that help students conduct a range of applications including web data scraping of popular social webs, text mining (e.g., word cloud, topic extraction, sentiment analysis), and data visualization. Students will explore the potential of digital media in storytelling, including VR, AR, XR, interactive storytelling, and data-driven narratives. The course equips students with the latest methods, techniques, and terminology for analyzing, interpreting, and appreciating digital media, while also fostering critical discussions about ethical considerations and the potential of these new media forms.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After completing the course, students will be able to:

3. Cultivate an understanding of emerging technologies in the cultural and creative industries.
4. Create compelling stories and scripts for immersive experiences. The skills learned can be applied in their careers to craft powerful messages, offer new perspectives, inspire action, and promote positive social change.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Public Relations and Social Theory
courses.description: Public relations is often studied and researched from marketing, business, communication management and functionalism perspectives. However, these perspectives do not suffice to understand its role in building, or destroying, trust, social legitimacy and reputation in the era of social media in which a ruthless comment, a 140-word microblog or a casual choice of words might trigger public reprimands and boycotts. As such, public relations should also be examined as a social phenomenon as well as a social activity in its own right and with its societal context. A more extensive use of social theories could help to provide analytical frameworks that highlight the consequences of public relations have for other actors and society as a whole. By applying the work of a group of prominent social theorists including Jürgen Habermas, Niklas Luhmann, Michel Foucault, etc, insights can be garnered for public relations studies at the macro, meso, and micro levels. Issues of how social power, behavior, and language exchanged or negotiated among various social actors in public relations phenomena will be intensively discussed in this course.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the conclusion of the course, students should have developed a deeper understanding and enhanced appreciation of social theories that could be brought to integrate in their daily practices. In particular, students are expected to have attained the following knowledge by the end of the course:

● A solid theoretical understanding of some of the classic social theories, including the key figures, concepts and developments.

● Application of theoretical perspectives to examining the public relations cases as social phenomena and social activities.

● Extended thinking ability as to how social theories could be applied to provide a constructive direction in the real practice of public relations in times of normalcy and crisis.

● Professional ethics and social legitimacy paradigm conducive to communicating messages to various actors in the society

● Commitment and passion towards professional development, intellectual curiosity and life-long learning.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Legal Issues in Public Relations and Advertising
courses.description:
This course aims to introduce students to key legal principles relevant to the fields of public relations and advertising. It provides a foundational understanding of the legal landscape that practitioners must navigate in their professional roles.
Students will explore several core areas of law that are most applicable to public relations and advertising, such as defamation, intellectual property, privacy, and regulatory compliance. Through real-world case studies and current legal controversies, students will gain practical insights into how legal issues can impact brand reputation, campaign effectiveness, and organizational credibility.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students should have developed a deeper understanding and enhanced appreciation of how legal principles intersect with public relations and advertising practices. Specifically, students will be able to:
i. Identify and explain the basic principles of law relevant to public relations and advertising, including:
• The elements that constitute a legal issue;
• The possible legal defenses available;
• The consequences of liability if found.

ii. Evaluate the risks associated with disclosing too much or too little information during a crisis, and understand the potential impact on both legal outcomes and public perception.

iii. Recognize legal red flags in public relations and advertising messages, and articulate specific elements that may expose practitioners or organizations to legal liability.

iv. Determine when and how to seek legal advice during a crisis, and assess the seriousness of legal counsel from a strategic communication perspective.

v. Apply legal reasoning to real-world case studies, enhancing their ability to make informed, ethical, and legally sound communication decisions.

courses.title: Special Topic in Creative and New Media I
courses.description: The instructor will lecture on and direct the study of a topic in Creative and New Media that he or she specializes in. Students are allowed to take this Special Topic course at most twice, and gain the units each time they pass the course. However, students cannot take courses with the same course code more than once in a single term.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Expected Learning Goals and Outcomes

1. Learn the skills of cultural research, the techniques of narrating stories and ideas.

2. Learn the tactics of writing columns and cultural criticism.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Digital Video Production
courses.description: This is a production-based course with an emphasis on hands-on learning. The course provides students with intensive training on digital storytelling techniques from cinematography, lighting to sound recording. Going through different stages of video-making from preproduction, production to postproduction, students will be able to understand the aesthetic reasoning behind visual production. They will learn how to communicate and tell a story via visual images.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking the course, students will be able to:
1) be more resourceful and knowledgeable about creativity and digital storytelling;
2) demonstrate a better technique in video making; and
3) acquire better understanding of the media industry.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Music Industry, Production and Marketing
courses.description: The course introduces Hong Kong popular music and the basic operations of the music industry. It covers a wide range of practical operation of record companies, including Artist and Repertoire Management, production of music and lyrics, marketing and sales, promotion and distribution. Besides the practical and management aspects, it also covers history and issues of popular music in Hong Kong, music commentary and the board theoretical, legal and social implications of the industry.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Expect Learning Goals and outcomes

KNOWLEDGE OUTCOMES

K1. Acquire a solid theoretical and practical basis for studying and analyzing Pop Music in Hong Kong as an everyday entertainment and cultural phenomena.

K2. Learn and apply theoretical and practical skills to convey informational, creative and persuasive messages in local and international Pop music/New Media contexts.

K3. To be equipped with specialized skills characteristic of the knowledge areas of marketing, promotion, lyrics writing, music-critic writing, A&R budgeting in Pop music industry and New Media in HK.

SPECIFIC SKILL OUTCOMES

S1. To be equipped with knowledge of lyrics writing, music-critic writing for becoming a lyricist or music critic.

S2. To be equipped with knowledge of marketing, promotion, A&R budgeting in Pop music industry/Records Co./New Media Entertainment fields.

S3. Information literacy for HK Pop music industry/Records Co./New Media Entertainment fields.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Film Directors
courses.description: This course will explore the "auteur" or "author" theory by focusing on several directors each time the course is offered. Auteur directors such as Alfred Hitchcock (希治閣), John Ford (約翰福特), Billy Wilder (比利懷德), Charlie Chaplin (卓別林), Akira Kurosawa (黑澤明), Francis Ford Coppola (哥普拉), Orson Welles (奧信威爾斯), Martin Scorcese (史高西斯), Zhang Yimou (張藝謀), Stanley Kwan (關錦鵬), Ann Hui (許鞍華),Wong Kar Wai (王家衛), Woody Allen (活地亞倫), Fellini (費里尼), Ingmar Bergman (柏格曼), Stanley Kubrick (寇比力克), Lars von Trier (查艾爾), etc., are among the possible choices for study in this course. Each semester the selection of directors will ensure a mix of past and present, as well as American, European and Asian filmmakers.
courses.learning_outcomes:
After taking this course, students are expected to:

1. Have deep understanding of the directors of the director’s key hole in filmmaking.

2. Acquire analytical skills to critique a film aesthetically and thematically through the prism of a director's vision.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Senior Research Project
courses.description: Students are required to finish a research project on selected topics related to current journalism and communication phenomena under the supervision of a faculty member The requirements include reviewing of literature, formulating research questions, data collection and report writing. Upon completion of this course, students shall be able to conduct a research and produce evidence in tackling a communication-related issue.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students should:
1. Learn the logic of research methods
2. Have the ability to conduct research
3. Have the ability to analyze research report critically
4. Have the ability to conduct in-depth independent study and self-learning
5. Have the ability to apply various research skills and to learn the professional attitudes and ethical standards to be researchers

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Global Digital Platforms: Culture, Power and Politics
courses.description: Platforms have become key technological, economic, and political actors in today's digital world. As digital platforms have increasingly been embedded in people’s daily lives, they have reshaped social connectivity, cultural tastes, media production, labor practices, and regulatory frameworks. This advanced course aims at introducing students to the key concepts, histories, and practices of global digital platforms from a multidisciplinary and comparative perspective.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Documentary
courses.description: This course explores the many varieties of documentary forms, from TV news and magazine features (both hard and soft) to stand-alone documentaries produced for television and film. Student groups will produce one short documentary during the semester.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Expected learning goals and outcomes:

The goal of the course is to increase students' competence in these areas by challenging you to produce documentary productions that are socially conscious and that use cutting edge presentational approaches so that viewers see issues in a new and challenging way.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Cinematography
courses.description: This course approaches cinematography from both technical and creative aspects. It explores aesthetics in film-making, with emphasis on camera work, lighting design and the roles of cinematographer. Students are expected to experiment with various components in both theory and practice through the course of study.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: COMM2922.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Expected Learning Goals and Outcomes:
1. Students can demonstrate professional skills required to operate small digital camera.
2. Acquire a solid theoretical and practical basis for cinematography.
3. Students can apply analytical theories, camera composition and lighting technique for a video shoot.
4. Solving problems that arise from practical shoots.
5. To analyze a script for principal photography.
6. To communicate well with all team members on a shoot.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advanced Photography
courses.description: This course is intended to advance photographic skills learned in previous courses to the professional level. Students are expected to have basic camera skills when they join the course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: COMM2440 or 2962.
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of this course, students are expected to be able to demonstrate advanced photographic skills such as specific photography techniques for products, protraits and scenery.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Topical Studies in Communication I
courses.description: Students concentrate their reading and study of one particular field in communication of their interests under the supervision of an instructor.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication or MA Journalism or MA Global Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students should gain a clear understanding of issues in that particular field in communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Topical Studies in Communication II
courses.description: Students concentrate their reading and study of one particular field in communication of their interests under the supervision of an instructor.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication or MA Journalism or MA Global Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students should gain a clear understanding of issues in that particular field in communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Emerging Global Media and Cultures
courses.description: This is a postgraduate class designed to acquaint students with the theories, trends, and debates of globalization from a media and cultural studies perspective. It explores the consequences and implications of globalization on media, culture, and society. Key theoretical texts will be read on a par with more empirically inspired texts, encouraging students to connect complex debates with concrete cultural imaginations and the objects and practices they generate.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.A. in Global Communication and M.Sc. in New Media students.
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students will be able to 1) articulate key concepts introduced to their daily experience of global media and cultural consumption; 2) critically evaluate the emerging practices and technologies in the global media industries; 3) develop a reflexive mindset sensitive to sustainability, diversity and inequalities in the process of cultural globalization.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Communication Theories I
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the current theories and concepts in media, technology, human, and global communication studies. It serves as an introduction to the current literature, main epistemologies, key theories, representative scholars and their works, and key sources of reference.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students will have gained a clear understanding of the major concepts and theories in the field of media and communication and obtained the intellectual skills to evaluate and critique those concepts and theories.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Writing for Research and Publication
courses.description: This course is designed for students to develop their research and academic writing skills pertaining to their theses and publications. The course is designed to help students learn best practices for how to turn an idea into a thesis and publishable research through making persuasive arguments through engaged writing.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students will have a clear understanding of researching for and structuring a thesis and research paper, including finding a good topic, asking relevant research questions, structuring an argument, providing persuasive evidence, and presenting all of those in writing.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Statistical Analysis in Communication
courses.description: This course aims at introducing graduate students to the study of the scientific discipline of communication. The course covers analyses of data using the general linear model. Topics include simple and multiple regression, analysis of variance and covariance, tests of significance, the interpretation of model parameters and other topics like path analysis and structural equation modeling as time allows. Students are expected to conduct a complete quantitative research and analysis at the end of the course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication or MA Global Communication

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Quantitative Communication Research
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to social scientific methods in communication research. It has two foci: 1) the epistemological and methodological principles of social science approach to communication; and 2) the skills in data handling. Issues covered including concept formation, hypothesis development, research design, sampling, and data gathering and analysis.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students should gain a clear understanding of the following:
• The logic of social scientific research in communication;
• Methods of framing research questions and techniques of gathering and interpreting empirical observations in an effort to answer a wide range of research questions; and
• The boundaries of the scientific approach to knowledge, the limits of quantitative methods in general, their techniques, assumptions, the strengths and weaknesses of particular methods and critiques of specific design.
Students should become more critical and discerning in their consumption of research findings; and are able to make appropriate problem/method(s) linkage in real-world settings.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Qualitative Communication Research
courses.description: This course is a graduate-level introduction to the qualitative methodology in communication. It will provide students with hands-on experiences with different approaches such as discourse analysis, ethnomethodology, ethnography and biographic method.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Public Relations Writing
courses.description: This course provides opportunity to students to develop proficient oral and written communication skills. Strategies for effective writing and presentation in the corporate world will be covered. Students will have multiple opportunities to demonstrate and to receive feedback on their professional communication style through classroon interaction, written assignments, and presentations.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising or MSSc Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to develop proficient written communication skills, and strategies for effective writing in the corporate communication world.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Public Relations Campaigns and Cases
courses.description: The course examines the development of public relations strategics and tactics by using actual public relations cases, events and campaigns. Public relations programmes directed toward employees, consumers, media, community, governmental officials and agencies, stockholders and other relevant groups are discussed and analyzed in the course. Students will be able to formulate strategies and tactics to achieve various public relations goals of the organization after completing the course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will build a deeper competency and understanding of real-world public relations practice and its nature. Students will be able to plan and execute strategic campaigns based on lessons learned from various international and local cases.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Investor Relations
courses.description: The course draws on case studies and professional experience to acquaint the students with the principles and practices of financial public relations. Stock market, financial and accounting knowledge is also explored in the course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to gain a clear understanding of the principles and practices of financial public relations. Stock market, financial and accounting knowledge is also explored in the course.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Applied Communication Research
courses.description: Introduction to applied media research, research criticism, data interpretation and fundamentals of audience analysis. Topics include: surveys, content analysis, experimental test of programmes, field research and formative evaluation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.A. in Global Communication, M.A. in Journalism, M.S.Sc. in Advertising, M.S.Sc. in Corporate Communication, M.Sc. in New Media students
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be familiarized with basic knowledge in conducting applied media research.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Corporate Communication
courses.description: Introduction to the theories, principles and practices of corporation communication. The focus of this course is on the investigation of communication processes and their application in the workplace. It is designed to familiarize students with the knowledge and skills essential to promote effective communication in a corporate setting. Topics include: corporate communication practice, corporate culture, corporate citizenship, relations with the media, crisis management and communication in global markets.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will acquire a clear understanding of basic concepts and principles of public relations in various organizational settings. They are expected to understand how public relations is strategic in nature, how organizations use communications to implement strategy, and how corporate communication relates to management and strategy in a corporation.

courses.title: Topical Studies in Corporate Communication II

Students are allowed to take the above topical studies courses for more than once, and gain the units each time they pass the course. However, students cannot take courses with the same course code more than once in a single term.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.S.Sc. in Corporate Communication and M.A. in Global Communication students.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Contextual Mood Management
courses.description: This course applies interpersonal and social theories in and for the context of public relations. By applying the work of a group of prominent interpersonal and social theorists, this course will explore together with students a different perspective to understand the public relations practices, processes and consequences/impact in the contemporary societies at the macro and micro levels. By crossing the paths and arenas between the interpersonal and public relations contexts, we will re-visit existing concepts and assumptions in the public relations context, and explore the new.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.S.Sc. in Corporate Communication students.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be cognizant of some conceptual blind spots of classical Public Relations theories and obtain an alternative perspective from the theoretical lens of interpersonal and social theories which better equip them in response to the ever-changing context.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Culture and Communication
courses.description: Culture drives social, political, and technological change. Alive and malleable, it constantly shifts with new forces, contexts, and contestations shaping everyday life. Culture and Communication approaches culture on two axes: first, what constitutes culture and how it shapes meaning and communication; second, how global crises and transformations redefine culture itself. Students examine cultural objects, practices, and phenomena—from viral trends and cinema to AI-generated media—to understand lived experiences and the politics of cultural regulation, including censorship, misinformation, and manipulation. The course foregrounds marginalized perspectives to foster ethical, responsible, and sensitive approaches to difference, dissonance, and intercultural exchange.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Corporate Communication or MA Global Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: This course introduces culture as both a site of inquiry and a methodological tool to understand today’s crises and conflicts. Students will engage in critical discourse analysis of everyday cultural objects, unpacking their social, political, and technological dimensions. Through an intersectional lens, they will explore how cultural objects are shaped by contestation, regulation, and global flows, and how these objects witness and influence our lives. The course emphasizes the politics embedded in cultural production and conflict while encouraging students to reflect on their ethical responsibility, positionality, and sensitivity to diversity in engaging with cultural practices and global cultural phenomena.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Conflict and Issue Management
courses.description: This course focuses on conflict and issue management in interpersonal, organizational, and inter-organizational relationships. The course content consists of theories related to conflict management and resolution, as well as those pertaining to issue management. Topics include the nature, identification, and analysis of conflicts and issues, communication and management aspects of conflicts and issues, strategies and tactics for conflict management, analysis of conflict styles, multi-party negotiations and coalition management in conflicts, issues management, and conflict resolution.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: This course is designed to help students develop abilities of inquiry, logical thinking, and critical analysis through the examination and application of theories and practices in conflict and issue management. Upon completing the course, students are expected to have competence in areas such as situational analysis of conflict and issues, planning strategies and tactics for conflict and issue management, assessing personal cognitive biases and conflict management styles, hands-on skills in negotiations and conflict resolution.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Chinese News Writing and Reporting
courses.description: This is an introductory course in Chinese news writing and reporting for the M.A. in Journalism students. Basic techniques of news reporting will be covered including: dealing with news sources, interviewing, library search and the use of electronic resources. The course also helps students develop various writing skills and familiarize them with different news formats.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be familiarized with basic techniques of news reporting and different news formats.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: English News Writing and Reporting
courses.description: This is an introductory course in English news writing and reporting for the M.A. in Journalism students. Basic techniques of news reporting will be covered including: dealing with news sources, interviewing, library search and the use of electronic resources. The course also helps students develop various writing skills and familiarize them with different news formats.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.A. in Journalism and M.A. in Global Communication students.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be familiarized with basic techniques of news reporting and different news formats.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Media Ethics and Law
courses.description: This course attempts to examine two essential confines of mass media communication, namely, the legal limits and ethical constraints. It covers major media laws and ethical issues that are related to the operation and practices of media organizations and practitioners.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Journalism or MSc New Media
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be knowledgeable of the essential concepts of media ethics and law; and its application through case studies. Students should also be able to reflect upon work related issues from a journalist’s perspective, and understand the values in ethics and importance of media law when doing news reporting and media-related work.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Financial Reporting and Writing
courses.description: Students will be able to understand basic financial knowledge. Students will learn to discover issues and report and write various kind of financial news, including finance, real estates, commercial and government financial policy writing, etc. The course will cover hot issues and topics in financial news, and students are expected to actively participate in discussion and reporting and writing.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in M.A. Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to understand basic financial knowledge; discover issues and report and write various kind of financial news; and understand how to handle the temptations in real life situations and different ethical issues.

courses.title: Beat Reporting in Technology, Health and Environment

courses.description: This course offers a unique opportunity to delve into the emerging beats that are paramount to society’s well-being: technology, health and environment. It will cover a wide range of topics, from artificial intelligence to cybersecurity, from medical breakthroughs to public health policies, and from climate change to environmental justice. The course will be divided into three modules on the three beats and taught by experienced journalists.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of M.A. in Journalism and M.A. in Global Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the key concepts, trends, and challenges in the fields of technology, health and the environment, including the latest advancements and emerging issues. They will acquire the necessary skills to gather, analyze and verify information related to the beats. They can explore potential career paths within the beats.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Infographics and Data Visualization
courses.description: This course explores data-based storytelling using charts, diagrams, maps, and other visualization techniques in professional communication. It covers theoretical topics such as principles of problem modeling, graphic design, and data processing. Additionally, practical issues like media form limitations and workflow challenges are discussed. Special emphasis is placed on ethical considerations and common pitfalls in data visualization.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For Students of M.A. in Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: After completing this course, students should be able to identify sources of useful data and assess its validity, analyze data to uncover stories, plan data-based storytelling through various forms of visualization, and design infographics and data visualizations that are not only attractive but also accurate and informative.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Analyzing Public Affairs
courses.description: Basic and background knowledge about a society’s political, economic, and social systems are essential for journalists working on public affairs. This class aims at equipping students with such basic and background knowledge and strengthening students’ capabilities in studying public affairs and policies. The class introduces students to fundamental concepts regarding the set up of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region – its government, its legal system, its economy, etc. It also discusses a few specific and “hot” policy issues.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.A. in Journalism and M.A. in Global Communication students
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to obtain relevant background knowledge to understand and analyze various public affairs that one may encounter as a journalist; critically evaluate public policies and social discussions related to the policies; to apply the relevant knowledge and concepts in the process of news-making.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Journalism Theory and Analysis
courses.description: This course introduces various theories in journalism and discusses important issues in the field. The scope of the course covers many aspects including the journalists their work organizations, their daily work routines, relationships between the press and other social institutions, news media and social environment, news culture, etc. Different conceptual approaches are used and various levels of analysis are also included.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication or MSSc Corporate Communication or MA Journalism or MA Global Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be familiarized with the use of empirical methods to examine existing knowledge of the news media—their character, behavior, policy and values; the nature of news; news content; news people; journalistic ethics; journalistic professionalism; and the impact of new technology on journalism.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Photography for Journalists
courses.description: In this course, students will learn news photography, photographic techniques for news reportage and the application of these techniques to foster visual communication. Photo elements, image editing and various visual approaches to news reportage will be examined.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be able to understand the visual approach to news reportage; apply photographic skills in news reportage; edit news photograph in computer; and acquire the taste to distinguish quality news photograph from the common.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Broadcast Journalism
courses.description: Theories and techniques of reporting, writing, editing, presenting and production of radio and television news will be introduced in this course. Students will acquire the essential skills to produce news magazines and bulletins for the electronic media.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected scrutinize radio and television news in broader perspectives and will have better understanding of the electronic media industry. They will also be able to develop insight for the future development of radio and TV news program; and acquire basic concepts of media convergence on electronic platforms.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Radio Studio Production
courses.description: This course introduces students to the role of radio broadcasting in the multimedia environment. Theories and practices of studio production of radio programmes including information, entertainment, documentaries and other programmes in new formats will be examined.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to understand the roles and duties of a responsible broadcaster; be capable of analyzing issues related to the radio broadcasting industry; and appreciate the aesthetics and master production techniques and skills required for a sound production.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Feature Writing
courses.description: This course seeks to instill students with the necessary skills to generate ideas for feature articles, compile information that is essential for the composition of these pieces, so as to be able to compose a wide variety of different features. Moreover, the course also aims at helping students to understand the ecology of the mass media from the views of a contributing journalist, both in terms of how to locate an outlet for their work, but also in how their work might (and would) become not only a tool with which readers understand the world, and whether their work would contribute to the "reproduction" of a hegemonic, "common-sensical" perspective of the state of the world.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.A. in Journalism and M.A. in Global Communication students.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to acquire the necessary skills to compose a wide variety of different features, as well as to understand the ecology of the mass media from the views of a contributing journalist.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Future of Journalism
courses.description: This course will analyze the challenges and opportunities presented by new technologies, changing audience behaviors, and shifting media landscapes. We will scrutinize important innovation cases and discuss the ways in which journalism can adapt to meet the needs of a changing world. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, guest talks, case studies and newsroom practices, the course emphasizes both the normative roles of journalism and a grounded understanding of what is really happening in the global journalism industry.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For Students of M.A. in Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: After taking the course, students will be able to analyze the current state of the journalism industry and develop a deep understanding of the challenges it faces; understand innovative technologies, business models, and news products in the journalism industry; keep up with important innovation cases in the industry and examine them with a critical perspective; develop skills necessary to succeed in the evolving field of journalism.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Seminar in Communication Theories
courses.description: It is a seminar designed to teach the major communication stream, disciplines, theories and thoughts. The content includes development of communication disciplines, analysis of major communication theories, case studies and applications.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.A. in Global Communication and M.A. in Journalism students
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to locate their own interests in communication theory for further study; discuss strengths and weaknesses of communication theories, ontology, and epistemology; reflect on their own and others’ individual, group, and relational identities and how those are enacted through communication in specific contexts; understand how ways of communicating and relating impact social interactions in f2f and virtual settings; analyze communication problems and opportunities in intercultural interactions; and understand how ways of communicating can marginalize and silence groups.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Reframing Narratives of the Global
courses.description: The global is a contested, evolving category that shapes how we understand ourselves, the world, and our futures. Its concept and lived experience diverge, demanding a critical vocabulary to see how it is mobilized, weaponized, and redefined amid poly-crises. Globalization is uneven, fragmented, and entangled with the local, marked by geopolitical and technological tensions. With the rise of planetary frameworks—climate justice, post-anthropocene thinking, more-than-human worlds—grappling with “the global” is urgent. This course explores eight dimensions of globalization, examining its metaphors, resistances, and underbellies to imagine sustainable, collective, and inclusive global narratives while fostering the capacity to critically engage and reframe them.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Global Communication
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students will:

* Critically understand how global narratives are produced and contested.
* Examine and develop theoretical perspectives to deconstruct and reimagine global approaches.
* Recognize alternative frameworks to address global challenges, including the SDGs.
* Develop strategies to analyze emerging crises and reframe them toward hope and impact.
* Build capacity to champion vulnerable and underserved communities in inequitable geographies.
* Connect critical theories to real-world interventions for collective, inclusive, and sustainable futures.
* Identify narrative framing techniques to influence and reshape global discourse.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Public Relations and Globalization
courses.description: This course addresses the topic of public relations in a globalized world. It will require frequent applications of what is discussed in class to analyze various current affairs topics, social and cultural issues and their relations with local and global business operations.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For MA in Global Communication, MSSc in Advertising and MSSc in Corporate Communication students
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to understand local and global stakeholders, their characteristics and the context they operate in; evaluate a PR proposal and pick out most of the elements that make a PR campaign successful; examine various factors that drive and shape public opinion and how they impact corporations, products and services, in particular those operating in Asia; manage a company/ organization's reputation and handle media relations through social media; and understand government relations in Asia.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Theories in Advertising and Communication
courses.description: This course first examines contemporary communication and behavioral theories of attitude and behavioral change, information processing and persuasion at the individual and sociological levels, then moves on to discuss their application to advertising and creative strategy decisions.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication or MSSc Advertising
courses.learning_outcomes: Students should be able to familiarize with existing and emerging academic advertising theories and their operating concepts and terms; identify the basic principles of advertising theories; create a logical and theoretical thinking pattern; develop competency in analyzing and understanding the elements of advertising theories; track the process of prediction and control in advertising communication; and apply the advertising theories in daily operations in the industry.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Creative Works: Appreciation and Strategy
courses.description: This course introduces to students the fundamentals of creative thinking with application to the production and execution of creative advertising strategies for the mass media. It is designed to develop in students the abilities to analyze, appreciate and critique past and existing advertising works, with an emphasis on research, ideation, selling and writing.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to develop the ability to analyze, appreciate and critique creative work within a strategic parameter; and practise by formulating and presenting a communication strategy and creating relevant creative work accordingly as teams.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Legal and Ethical Aspects in Advertising
courses.description: This course examines the legal and ethical constraints that affect the production, contents and placement of advertising in the mass media. In regard to the former, case laws and ordinances related to advertising in the print and electronic media will be discussed. As far as the latter is concerned, common ethical problems and issues in advertising will be examined. Case studies will be used as illustrations in both.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to understand the advertising regulatory forces in the States; the advertising regulatory bodies and laws in Hong Kong and the Greater China; identify and explore major ethical controversies in the field of advertising; develop a position on essential ethical issues; and apply the legal and ethical principles in campaign projects.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Mastering Digital Media Content
courses.description: This course examines the latest trends of content making of marketing communications in digital and social space. Students will gain an in-depth knowledge of how to develop, explore, and appreciate different creative techniques, while crafting creative content for effective communication.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For Students of M.A. in Global Communication, M.S.Sc. in Advertising and M.S.Sc. in Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to advance their understandings in creative techniques; be able to employ different tactics in content making; be able to experiment and advance their role as content creator.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Applied Advertising Copywriting
courses.description: This course advances students to apply idea generation and copywriting techniques to select categories of advertising products for a comprehensive range of communication channels. Other executional elements such as the musical and visual elements in advertising will also be enhanced.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will develop solid copywriting and thinking skills that they will find useful in real working environment.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Branding in China
courses.description: This advanced branding course investigates strategic approaches for brand development within and beyond the Chinese market. It emphasizes an understanding of Chinese consumers, both locally and globally, and explores how local and Western brands can establish a pertinent presence.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For Students of M.S.Sc. in Advertising and M.S.Sc. in Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon completion, students will have mastered strategic branding techniques for the Chinese market, obtained profound insights into Chinese consumer behaviour, and learnt how to differentiate brands in a competitive environment. The course aims to equip students with the skill set required to become proficient brand strategists, capable of creating and managing brands effectively within the Chinese market context.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Advanced Advertising Art Direction
courses.description: This course covers advanced principles and theories of art direction and design in the advertising industry. Students will develop an in-depth understanding of conceptual, technical, aesthetic and communicative skills in visual advertising. They will learn to develop, appreciate and evaluate creative visual ideas for advertising campaigns.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to be knowledgeable about the creative role and tasks of an art director; be able to originate creative concepts, especially visual concepts; be able to visualize, execute and present ad proposals and campaigns; be knowledgeable about production, creative techniques, tools and resources.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: New Media Business Model and Innovation
courses.description:
This course prepares students to become digital product/service operation professionals, digital marketing specialists, UX researchers/designers, and startup founders by integrating business models, user experience, and technology platforms in developing and managing digital products.
Throughout the course, special attention will be given to new media project operation so that students can gain hands-on knowledge and skills to plan and deploy new media products from start to finish.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc New Media
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students are expected to be familiarized with but not limited to the following topics:
1. The User Experience Perspective
2. New Media Product Development
3. Business Strategy and Model for Sustainability and Growth
4. Digital Marketing and Analytics
5. Business Valuation for a New Media Venture

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: New Communication Technologies: Trends and Impacts
courses.description: This course is designed to examine varying theoretical perspectives related to the future trends and current uses and impacts of information technologies and services. The course provides a foundation from which students can conceptualize the factors that lead people to use communication technologies, the needs that these technologies fulfill, and the effects of such use on individuals, organizations and society.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication or MSc New Media or MSSc Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to gain a clear understanding of theoretical perspectives related to the future trends, current uses and impacts of information technologies and services.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: New Media Content Development
courses.description: This course focuses on how to conceive and create interactive information and entertainment multimedia content for the Internet. The major emphasis of this course will be on interactive thinking and advanced multimedia production technique and other skills.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc New Media
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to understand how to develop relevant new media content that support meaningful and interactive experience for different applications and purposes; how users conceive traditional and interactive multimedia content for the Internet; the use of different content types from user experience and strategic point of views; and develop ability to develop and implement a unified content strategy.
