courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: New Media Analytics
courses.description: This course introduces practical measurement and analytics framework not only to help businesses to measure success, but also to make better decisions that will optimize business value creation. Key topics include measurement approaches, KPIs, processes, tools, testing and optimization methodologies.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For M.Sc. in New Media students
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will acquire knowledge in the key concepts, frameworks and terminology of measurement and analytics, and approaches to evaluate analytics; develop ability to analyze problems, conduct necessary research and determine the best approach for the problem; and be able to apply analytics methodologies into real-world situations, and to optimize value creation of using new media channels.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: New Media Ecology
courses.description: This course introduces students to the role of content flow and value chain model in the information industry. It covers various topics such as content creation, selling, distribution, syndication, consumption, content economics, business models, related technology and copyright protection issues faced by different information industries in the new media ecology.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Journalism or MSc New Media
courses.learning_outcomes: Students should gain a clear understanding of newspaper publishing, periodical publishing, book publishing, music, radio, TV, video, games, telecommunications and the web from the new media perspective and how these things work in the new media ecology.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Independent Studies in Communication
courses.description: Students conduct an independent research project under the supervision of an instructor.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication or PhD Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students should complete the independent research project.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Topical Studies in Communication IV
courses.description: Students concentrate their reading and study of one particular field in communication of their interests under the supervision of an instructor.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For MPhil Communication or PhD Communication or MA Global Communication students.
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students should gain a clear understanding of issues in that particular field in communication.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Communication Theories II
courses.description: This course provides an advanced engagement with media, technology, human, and global communication studies. It introduces students to selective theories, concepts, and debates, representative scholars, and the arguments of their work.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For PhD Communication or MPhil Communication students.
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students will have become familiar with the theories and concepts addressed in this course and able to evaluate and critique the theories, concepts, and findings of scholarly work in an advanced way.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Digital Research
courses.description: How has the rise of digital media, new data landscape, and computational tools transformed the process of knowledge generation and academic production? In preparing students to engage with this digital social and research environment, this course has three interrelated foci: (1) To introduce epistemological and ontological perspectives on the concepts of data, analytics, and knowledge production; (2) To discuss emerging theoretical approaches to studying digital media-rich phenomenon; (3) To provide basic training on selecting digital data analytic tools and techniques, with an aim to incorporate these skills in research projects.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in PhD Communication; or MPhil Communication
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
- Understand the key notions of “data,” “digital media” and “digitization” at a theoretical and epistemological level
- Know how the computer works and understand the popular algorithms for social sciences
- Conceive and design digital research projects from a communication studies or broadly defined social science perspective
- Understand the applicability and limitations of conventional research methods in the digital arena.
- Take up basic ideas and skills of digital research such as data mining and data visualization.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Strategies for Integrated Communication Campaigns
courses.description: This course covers concepts and theories of social change, attitude change, diffusion of innovation, development and underdevelopment, and modernization. Students will be trained to do research in these areas and be able to apply communication theories and research methods in designing, executing and evaluating specific campaigns.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of M.S.Sc. in Advertising, M.S.Sc. in Corporate Communication, M.A. in Global Communication and M.Sc. in New Media
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will gain understanding on various communication theoretical formations pertinent to campaign message development; acquire IMC concepts and tools and their applications in various campaign efforts; identify effective campaign elements contributing to the success of integrated communication campaigns; and equip students with a working knowledge of campaign design, implementation and evaluation.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Practicum in Journalism
courses.description: This is a dynamic and practical course designed to simulate the actual environment of a professional newsroom. This immersive experience aims to bridge the gap between classroom learning and the real world of journalism. Students will participate in press conferences, conduct interviews, and produce news content across various platforms including course website and social media accounts. The course provides a unique opportunity for students to apply their journalistic skills and ethics in a practical, hands-on setting, and build up their portfolio.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For Students of M.A. in Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon completion of this course, students will be able to understand the workings of a real-world newsroom, apply theoretical knowledge to practice, demonstrate proficiency in journalistic writing and reporting, collaborate effectively in a team environment, and develop a portfolio of journalistic work.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: Students concentrate their reading and study of one particular topic in Journalism of their interests under the supervision of a faculty member. Students are required to submit a paper at the end of the course.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Journalism
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students engage in either a journalistic project or an academic project. In the former case, the students should plan, develop, and execute a piece of in-depth feature coverage of a chosen topic under the supervision of a teacher. In the latter case, the students should plan, design, and execute an academic study on a topic related to journalism under the supervision of a faculty member. Students are required to submit a substantial journalistic report in the former case and a paper in the latter case at the end of the course.

The students are expected to acquire critical thinking and analytical ability; gain the experience of engaging in a long-term journalistic project or an academic research project; gain an in-depth understanding on a special topic (a public affairs topic in the case of a journalistic project and an academic topic within the field of journalism studies in the case of an academic project).

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Channel Planning and Performance Media
courses.description: This course familiarizes students with the concepts of channel planning and performance media, including the use and analysis of data related to consumer behavior, media usage and audience insights, the development of a media plan, strategy development, media buying and budgeting in various channels like internet, TV and outdoor etc through real-life applications and case studies.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to have a clear understanding of the role and structure of a media agency; media landscape in HK; market, proprietary and tailor-made research; how to reach target effectively; display ad and search engine marketing; social media, mobile and other digital platforms; and creative media buy.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Consumer Behaviour and Audience Analysis
courses.description: This course provides students with an understanding of the mental, emotional and physical activities that people engage in when selecting, purchasing and disposing of products and services so as to satisfy needs and desires. It will also introduce to students techniques for conducting and interpreting audience analysis, with a focus on demographic and psychographic methods used in the advertising industry.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising or MSSc Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to gain a clear understanding of consumer behavior from both a macro (sociological) and micro (psychological) perspectives; and different strategic analysis techniques and tools for inquiring consumer mind and behavior.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Account Planning and Advertising Management
courses.description: This course helps students approach account servicing from multiple points of references, such as agency, client and media, with the emphasis on a communication plan that integrates all elements of the promotional mix – advertising, personal selling, public relations, sales promotion, direct response and interactive marketing – into a total strategic package that results in maximum impact.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Advertising
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to understand what effective account planning is all about and the changing face of account planning in the digital age; apply account planning thinking mode and practices to any broad-based or brand-based, integrated marketing communications tasks in the real world settings; identify the key attributes and professional expectations required for being an outstanding account planner in action.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Brand Strategy and Integrated Marketing Communication
courses.description: With a business and competitive landscape complicated by social challenges, media fragmentation, new technologies, and polarized consumer opinions, brands must keep abreast of the fast-changing environment to have relevant presence and behaviour. It is important to have a brand strategy that truly connects and has the potential to create behavioural changes. This course puts focus back on the basics, and align with the students on some of the core concepts on marketing communications, before developing any integrated marketing campaign that would otherwise become just a blinkered approach to multifaceted problems.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For Students of M.S.Sc. in Advertising and M.S.Sc. in Corporate Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will learn to develop brand strategy with sharpness by asking the right questions, investigating new perspectives, and define what we want people to do, before we are over excited with various tactics and rush to put together campaign. We develop works that work, and not noise in the market.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Graduation Project
courses.description: Students are required to complete a Graduation Project on an approved topic under close supervision of a faculty member to demonstrate what they have learned from the program. The project can be in the form of a systematic research, a formative evaluation of a media campaign, or a case study.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Global Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: By the end of the course, students should complete their graduation projects.

courses.subject: COMM
courses.title: Directed Study in New Media Project
courses.description: This is an interactive workshop for students to produce advanced interactive multimedia or conduct an in-depth research on selected new media topics as their graduation projects.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSc New Media
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to complete their graduation projects.

courses.description: Thesis preparation by M. Phil. students will be closely monitored by the thesis supervisor in order to ensure satisfactory completion of the thesis.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil Communication
courses.learning_outcomes: Students are expected to make progress in their thesis at the end of the course.
